fields.features_heading: What a Write-Up Needs Before Anyone Signs
fields.features_subheading: Describe your policy and who signs off. Emergent builds the form managers file, the HR review behind it, and the records HR keeps.
fields.feature_1:
Facts first, conclusions left out

Ask for the date, the policy broken, and what the manager saw or heard firsthand. A required field for the expected change and the next step keeps vague wording off the page.
fields.feature_2:
Earlier warnings, already on the page

Pick the employee and the form lists their past write-ups with date, policy, and level. The app then suggests the next step on your discipline ladder for the manager to confirm.
fields.feature_3:
HR reads it before the meeting

Write-ups at the final warning level wait for HR approval before delivery. HR gets an email or Slack alert that one is waiting, with a link and no personal details in it.
fields.feature_4:
The employee has a say, then signs

Give the employee a box for their own account, then a signature line that confirms receipt, not agreement. If they decline to sign, the manager marks it and a witness signs.
fields.feature_5:
Review dates that come back around

Each improvement plan carries goals and a review date. The manager gets a reminder 3 days before it, and closes the plan or moves to the next step from the same record.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and run the form beside your HR system. Keep changing it by prompt after export, or edit the code yourself.

plan.angle: The results for this query are blank Word and PDF write-up templates plus HR blog guides that list the fields. None shows what happens around the form: the earlier warnings a manager has to dig up, HR reading the write-up before it is delivered, the employee's own statement and signature, and the review date on the improvement plan. This page shows a working write-up form for four moments (attendance, a safety violation, the signing meeting, HR follow-up), with every write-up saved to a database the employer owns. No legal advice; the one retention fact quotes the EEOC.
tab_stories: At Wickerby Diner, shift manager Paula Gorsky files a write-up for server #118's third late arrival in 90 days; the form shows the 2 verbal warnings already on file and sets the level to written warning.

At Boxwood Freight, supervisor Marcus Dellacorte writes up forklift operator #2214 for driving without a seat belt, attaches 2 photos and policy 4.2, and because it is the second safety write-up in 12 months the form makes it a final written warning that HR reviews before delivery.

At Hollisdale Dental, employee #431 reads the write-up on the office tablet, adds a short statement in their own words and signs a line that confirms receipt, not agreement; office manager Gwen Cassidy countersigns.
At Strathorne Fitness, HR lead Owen Nettleton tracks 14 open write-ups across 5 clubs, each with a 30-day review date; 3 reviews are due this week and one is 4 days overdue.
